slides.title: Stop sorting your doom pile. Do this instead.
Why sorting fails
slides.body: Sorting asks for 100 tiny decisions in a row. Our brains run out of decisions around item 12. Then the pile wins.

slides.title: Pull out the easy stuff first
slides.body: Trash and dishes only. No thinking required. The pile shrinks fast and you get a hit of momentum.

slides.title: Then things with a home
slides.body: If you know where it lives without thinking, put it there. If you have to think, it stays.

slides.title: The rest goes in one 'decide' box
slides.body: Put a date on it. Look at it once a week for 10 minutes. Most of it will be easy by then.

slides.title: Find out why it piles there
slides.body: A pile on the counter means stuff needs a home near the counter. Add a tray or bin right there.

slides.title: A doom pile is a list of decisions my brain postponed. Not a moral failure.
Dismantle every doom pile in your house
slides.body: The full doom-pile method is in The Messy Brain Home Reset. Link in bio.
